locations.name: Sepulveda Tunnel
locations.description: Riders on horseback and early automobiles crowded the road at this tunnel in 1930. Compare that scene with the same approach in 2026.
locations.accessibility: Busy traffic route through the Sepulveda Pass. Enjoy the view safely and do not stop in the tunnel or traffic lanes.
locations.thenAlt: 1930: Riders on horseback and early automobiles at the Sepulveda tunnel.

locations.name: Sherman Oaks Circle
locations.address: Sherman Oaks Circle, south of Ventura Blvd. near Sepulveda Blvd.
locations.description: The Sherman Oaks Circle, laid out just south of Ventura Boulevard, seen around 1940 with young cypress trees and open hills beyond. A 1929 plan for a “City Hall” here was never built; a short street still carries the circle’s name.
locations.accessibility: Residential street. Please view from the public sidewalk.
locations.thenAlt: Around 1940: A traffic circle ringed with young cypress trees, with open hills beyond.

locations.name: Ventura and Sepulveda
locations.description: A Mobil station and a neighborhood market beside the new San Diego Freeway (405) in the 1960s, compared with the same corner from the air in 2026.
locations.accessibility: Busy intersection beside the 405 freeway. Both views are aerial photographs.
locations.thenAlt: 1960s: Aerial view of Ventura and Sepulveda with a Mobil station beside the 405 freeway.
locations.nowAlt: 2026: Aerial view of Ventura and Sepulveda beside the 405 freeway.

locations.name: La Reina Theatre
locations.description: The La Reina opened on Ventura Boulevard in 1937. Compare a 1945 view of the theatre with the corner today, where the building is home to shops.
locations.accessibility: Private businesses. Please view the building from the public sidewalk.
locations.thenAlt: 1945: The La Reina Theatre sign and marquee on Ventura Boulevard.
locations.nowAlt: 2026: The former La Reina Theatre building with shop signs.

locations.name: Casa de Cadillac
locations.description: Opened in 1949 as Don Lee Cadillac and renamed Casa de Cadillac in 1950. Compare the showroom at Christmas 1955 with 2025.
locations.accessibility: Private business. Please view the showroom from the public sidewalk.
locations.thenAlt: Christmas 1955: The Casa de Cadillac showroom lit up at night.
locations.nowAlt: 2025: The Casa de Cadillac showroom at dusk.

locations.name: Fashion Square and the Ventura Freeway
locations.description: Fashion Square opened in 1962 beside the Ventura Freeway, on the former McKinley Home for Boys site. A historic aerial view to compare with 2026 is being prepared.
locations.accessibility: Shopping center open to the public.
locations.nowAlt: 2026: Aerial view of Westfield Fashion Square and the Ventura Freeway.

locations.name: Casa Vega
locations.description: Part of Ventura Boulevard since 1956. Compare a 1970 aerial view of the corner of Fulton Avenue with the same corner in 2026.
locations.accessibility: Private business. Both views are aerial photographs.
locations.thenAlt: 1970: Aerial view of Casa Vega at Ventura Boulevard and Fulton Avenue.
locations.nowAlt: 2026: Aerial view of Casa Vega on Ventura Boulevard.
